title: Perioperative Hyperglycemia
sources: ADA. Diabetes Care in the Hospital: Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1):S339-S351
Raiten JM et al. Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors. J Cardiothorac Vasc Anesth 2024;38:57-66
Multisociety Clinical Practice Guidance for Safe Use of GLP-1 RAs in the Perioperative Period. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2024

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV perioperative hyperglycemia guide. Targets, treatment threshold, and the medication-hold table incl. the reversed 2024 GLP-1 guidance.

summary: Target 100–180 mg/dL; treat sustained values > 180. Tighter than ~80–180 has no clear outcome advantage and a real hypoglycemia cost. Screen everyone — ~1/3 of hospital hyperglycemia occurs with no prior diabetes diagnosis, and that group carries the higher mortality signal. Frame it as physiologic stability, not glycemic perfection.

items: Target range 100–180 mg/dL (ADA Standards of Care). Trigger treatment for sustained values > 180, not the first isolated elevated reading.
Do not chase tighter control in the OR — goals stricter than ~80–180 have not shown an outcome advantage and add hypoglycemia risk.

Hyperglycemia is part of the mechanism doing the damage — impaired neutrophil function and phagocytosis, osmotic diuresis with volume shifts, electrolyte derangement, and endothelial injury all track with the glycemic excursion.

rows: Individualize to intake and measured glucose
Continue at 50–80% of the usual dose
Euglycemic DKA risk — FDA and multispecialty guidance
The 2023 ASA blanket-hold recommendation was reversed in late 2024; current multisociety guidance favors continuation for most, with attention to residual gastric contents / aspiration risk

body.text: The undiagnosed-diabetes group matters: an elevated glucose with no chronic adaptation behind it reflects a more acute, less-buffered physiologic insult — screen everyone perioperatively, not just known diabetics.
